questions.q: Which of these is part of the formal definition of an asset?
options: It must be something the business has already sold
It must be a physical object that can be touched
It must have cost the business no money to acquire
It is a resource controlled by the business, from a past transaction, expected to provide future economic benefit
questions.explain: An asset is a resource the business controls, arising from a past transaction, that is expected to provide future economic benefit.

questions.q: Why can a business record a leased piece of equipment as an asset, even though it does not legally own it?
options: Because leased equipment is always classified as a liability instead
Because the asset definition is based on control, not strict legal ownership
Because leases are never recorded in accounting at all
Because only purchased equipment counts, and leases are an exception with no rule
questions.explain: The asset definition hinges on control of the resource, not necessarily outright legal ownership.

questions.q: What distinguishes a current asset from a noncurrent asset?
options: Current assets are always worth less than $1,000
Current assets are only cash itself; everything else is noncurrent
Current assets are expected to convert to cash or be used up within about a year; noncurrent assets provide benefit longer than that
There is no meaningful distinction between the two
questions.explain: The current/noncurrent split is based on how quickly the asset is expected to convert to cash or be consumed.

questions.q: Why is Inventory classified as a current asset, even though it may physically sit in a warehouse for weeks?
options: Because the test for current vs. noncurrent is expected speed to cash through sale, not physical appearance
Because inventory never actually appears on a balance sheet
Because inventory is technically a liability, not an asset
Because warehouses are always considered noncurrent
questions.explain: Inventory is expected to be sold and converted to cash within the normal operating cycle, which makes it current despite sitting in a warehouse.

questions.q: Which Oracle Fusion Financials module exists specifically to track noncurrent assets like equipment and buildings, including their depreciation?
options: Oracle Fusion Receivables
Oracle Fusion Cash Management
Oracle Fusion Payables
Oracle Fusion Assets (Fixed Assets)
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Assets (Fixed Assets) is the module dedicated to tracking noncurrent assets and their depreciation over time.
